Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

Class CertificatePrincipalExtractor

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509.CertificatePrincipalExtractor
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.security.web.authentication.preauth.x509.X509PrincipalExtractor
public class CertificatePrincipalExtractor extends Object implements org.springframework.security.web.authentication.preauth.x509.X509PrincipalExtractor
Takes the SHA-256 fingerprint of the client certificate as the principal, as 64 lower case hexadecimal digits, which is what a binding stores and what ResolveCertificateLoginUseCase looks up. The fingerprint, and not the subject name, identifies a certificate: whoever controls a CA can issue a certificate with any subject, and none with a given fingerprint. A certificate that is expired or not yet valid has no principal: neither the TLS handshake of the dedicated port (no authority validates the chain) nor a proxy that forwards a certificate is trusted to have checked it. One extractor serves both transports, because both leave the certificate in the same request attribute.
